spec_match.rationale: Probes the proposal's one concrete new surface (entryType 'session-end' in supportedEntryTypes), demonstrates the exact failure class the explainer's use cases describe (abrupt termination losing final telemetry), and shows the shipped mitigation (fetchLater) the guidance recommends.

interactive.rationale: Three real experiments: a supportedEntryTypes probe that prints the browser's actual list, a worker graceful-vs-terminate() comparison with a results table, and a real fetchLater() deferred beacon.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb names the three experiments; the page delivers all three.

edge_cases.rationale: Missing PerformanceObserver, missing Worker, and missing fetchLater each get labelled fallbacks that never report fake success; the probe can return true if a future browser ships session-end.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/6594955352080384, the explainer's use-cases section, and MDN fetchLater.

conformance.rationale: The session-end-entry-type-proposed assertion in the feature suite mirrors this page's probe exactly, including the expected-fail framing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: probe printed 13 real entry types without session-end; graceful run delivered 5 progress + final, terminate() run delivered 3 progress and provably lost the final message; fetchLater() returned {activated:false}; zero console errors and no failed requests; screenshots inspected.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the probe ran, both worker outcomes (graceful delivered / abrupt lost), and fetchLater scheduling or fallback.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; the delivered/lost verdicts use accent-emerald/accent-rose on the near-white paper background (AA for large bold text).

accessibility.rationale: Results table has a proper thead/scope structure and aria-label; every result panel is role=status; buttons are native and 44px tall.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: responsive-check matrix ok on both classes; the three stages stack cleanly at 360px with no overflow.

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate delivered fetchLater beacon end-to-end
openQuestions.detail: Scheduling is verified ({activated:false}), but delivery could not be observed because the harness SIGKILLs the whole browser process, which is outside fetchLater's guarantee. A manual pass should navigate away normally and confirm the beacon lands at ../report.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use fetchLater() for reliable end-of-session telemetry: schedule early, abort-and-reschedule on updates, let the browser own delivery; wrap calls in try/catch for quota errors.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Stage 3 implements exactly this pattern (AbortController re-scheduling, try/catch, browser-owned delivery) and the page copy explains why it is today's best answer.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Convey pass/fail state with text, not colour alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The delivery table verdicts say 'yes — final message arrived' / 'NO — final message lost' in addition to the green/red colouring.

summary: Verified with headless Chromium 141 over CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud routine): all three experiments exercised for real — the probe lists the browser's actual entry types, the terminate() run demonstrably loses the worker's final message while the graceful run delivers it, and fetchLater() schedules a real deferred beacon. Console and network clean on desktop and mobile.
